mechanism.owner_quote: Publish-subscribe is a delivery contract, not a fire-and-forget call.
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: Record whether it is ephemeral or durable before claiming a guarantee.
invariant.reason: Abridged page has no durability or delivery-guarantee prose.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Redelivery follows an effect that committed before its acknowledgement; the opposite order loses work.
failure_recovery.reason: Page has no ack-ordering or redelivery recovery text.

alternative.owner_quote: Use ephemeral pub/sub only when losing a signal with no listener is acceptable; a durable business task needs a persisted consumer or queue.
alternative.reason: Page has no comparison or selection guidance.

mechanism.owner_quote: One message has one eligible worker at a time
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: The queue contract must state its ordering scope and terminal path for poison messages.
invariant.reason: Page states single-receiver delivery only, no ordering or terminal rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A worker crash after the effect but before acknowledgement can cause redelivery
failure_recovery.reason: Page has no crash, ack, redelivery or duplicate text.

alternative.owner_quote: When one task has one natural owner, direct request/response or a shared log may avoid brokered indirection; fan-out fits when several independent subscribers need a copy.
alternative.reason: Page links related patterns without comparison.

mechanism.owner_quote: Several consumers read from one queue, and each message is delivered to one of them so the work is processed in parallel.
mechanism.reason: Defines multiple consumers sharing one queue with one delivery per message.

invariant.owner_quote: Acknowledgment must follow the durable business effect, and redelivery after a missing acknowledgment must not duplicate that effect.
invariant.reason: Page has no ack, dedup or idempotency requirement.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A slow or poisoned message blocks progress through visibility timeouts and repeated redelivery; bound attempts and route permanently failing work to a declared terminal path.
failure_recovery.reason: Page has no visibility-timeout, poison or terminal path.

alternative.owner_quote: Partitioned consumers own a stable key range and preserve per-key order; prefer competing consumers when order is not required and pool parallelism is the goal.
alternative.reason: Contrasts partitioned consumers that preserve per-key order.

mechanism.owner_quote: A push subscription hands each message to the consumer; the handler, not a polling loop, decides when work is acknowledged.
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: It must own effect identity, deduplication and acknowledgement ordering
invariant.reason: Page defines delivery/callback but not consumer-owned dedup or ack ordering.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A crash between effect and acknowledgement leaves the outcome unknown; acknowledging before the effect can lose work.
failure_recovery.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

alternative.owner_quote: Polling a queue or a scheduled batch job may be preferable when volume is low, batch control matters or the consumer cannot own a cursor.
alternative.reason: Page links Polling Consumer without comparison.

mechanism.owner_quote: A requester sends a message with a reply address and a correlation value, and the responder returns a message that the requester matches to the original request.
mechanism.reason: Defines a reply address and correlation value matched to the request.

invariant.owner_quote: A reply must correlate to exactly one outstanding request and must not be processed as a new command by another consumer.
invariant.reason: Requires one outstanding request per correlation value and no command reinterpretation.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A lost request or reply leaves an unresolved operation; expose the outstanding request record, apply a reply deadline and reconcile before retrying.
failure_recovery.reason: Page has crash/restart but no lost-request record or reply deadline.

alternative.owner_quote: Synchronous RPC with a deadline is simpler when the responder is reachable and the work fits the request budget; choose messaging when availability or latency requires decoupling.
alternative.reason: Contrasts synchronous RPC with messaging for availability or latency decoupling.

mechanism.owner_quote: A correlation identifier ties together messages that belong to one request, workflow or conversation.
mechanism.reason: Defines an identifier tying messages to one request, workflow or conversation.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs a generation rule, propagation across asynchronous boundaries, a retention window and a collision check.
invariant.reason: Requires generation, propagation, retention and collision rules.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is a lost or duplicated identifier; carry it in the message contract and record it at every boundary.
failure_recovery.reason: Page defines IDs only; no lost/duplicate or failure path.

alternative.owner_quote: A transport-native message identity is the alternative when the broker guarantees the needed scope and lifetime.
alternative.reason: Page lists related patterns without alternative comparison.

mechanism.owner_quote: A content-based router chooses a destination from message content.
mechanism.reason: Defines destination selection from message content.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs a versioned predicate set, a default or dead-letter path and an owner for rule changes.
invariant.reason: Page has maintainability prose but no versioned predicate set or rule owner.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is an unmatched or misrouted message; route to a declared fallback and record the predicate version.
failure_recovery.reason: Names unmatched or misrouted messages and requires fallback plus predicate version recording.

alternative.owner_quote: A workflow/orchestrator is the alternative when routing needs multiple steps or compensations; do not hide a process engine inside the router.
alternative.reason: Page has no workflow or process-engine alternative.

mechanism.owner_quote: A message filter evaluates a predicate and forwards only matching messages to a consumer, discarding the rest by policy.
mechanism.reason: Defines predicate-based forwarding and policy discard.

invariant.owner_quote: Every discarded message must be an intentional drop under a versioned predicate, not an unobserved loss.
invariant.reason: Requires intentional drops under a versioned predicate rather than unobserved loss.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Predicate drift or a missing default path silently removes traffic; monitor filter rates and keep a declared fallback for unmatched messages.
failure_recovery.reason: Page has no drift, filter-rate monitoring or unmatched fallback.

alternative.owner_quote: A content-based router sends different subsets to different destinations; prefer filtering when the destination is the same and only selection changes.
alternative.reason: Contrasts a router that sends subsets to different destinations.

mechanism.owner_quote: Pipes and filters decompose processing into ordered, replaceable stages connected by a message contract.
mechanism.reason: Defines ordered replaceable stages connected by a message contract.

invariant.owner_quote: Each stage needs its own failure and retry policy, and the pipeline needs backpressure, a rule for partial completion and a declared ordering scope.
invariant.reason: Page has no per-stage failure, backpressure or partial-completion rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is a failed middle stage with earlier effects already applied; record stage identity and compensate or replay from a declared checkpoint.
failure_recovery.reason: Page has no failed-middle-stage or checkpoint recovery.

alternative.owner_quote: A single in-process transformation is the alternative when the stages are small and cannot be operated independently.
alternative.reason: Page names no single in-process transformation alternative.

mechanism.owner_quote: A splitter turns one input into several independently processable messages.
mechanism.reason: Defines one input becoming several processable messages.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs part identity, per-part idempotency, a completion or compensation rule and a bounded fan-out.
invariant.reason: Camel documents part index/complete/size but not per-part idempotency or fan-out bound.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is a split that produces only some parts; record part identity and completion, then retry missing parts without duplicating completed effects.
failure_recovery.reason: Requires partial-split recording and retry of missing parts without duplicating completed effects.

alternative.owner_quote: A single consumer with internal fan-out is the alternative when the parts are small and atomicity is required.
alternative.reason: Page does not compare single-unit processing or single-consumer fan-out.
